 A fine away performance, and a bit of luck, saw Arsenal emerge from Barcelona with a precious Champions League point
  Updated  1h ago Simon Burnton Thu 12 Nov 2026 15.07 EST First published on Thu 12 Nov 2026 12.00 EST Share Key events 2h ago Final score: Barcelona 1-1 Arsenal 
 2h ago GOAL! Barcelona 1-1 Arsenal (Graham Hansen, 59 mins) 
 3h ago Half time: Barcelona 0-1 Arsenal 
 3h ago GOAL! Barcelona 0-1 Arsenal (Maanum, 22 mins) 
 4h ago Preamble 
 4h ago The teams! 
 Barcelona's Caroline Graham Hansen fire home to restore parity. Photograph: Albert Gea/Reuters View image in fullscreen Barcelona's Caroline Graham Hansen fire home to restore parity. Photograph: Albert Gea/Reuters Simon Burnton Thu 12 Nov 2026 15.07 EST First published on Thu 12 Nov 2026 12.00 EST Share Key events 2h ago Final score: Barcelona 1-1 Arsenal 
 2h ago GOAL! Barcelona 1-1 Arsenal (Graham Hansen, 59 mins) 
 3h ago Half time: Barcelona 0-1 Arsenal 
 3h ago GOAL! Barcelona 0-1 Arsenal (Maanum, 22 mins) 
 4h ago Preamble 
 4h ago The teams! 
 1h ago 15.07 EST And with that, I’ll be on my way. Here’s that match report again. Bye!
 Arsenal dig deep to earn WCL draw in face of Barcelona dominance Read more Share 1h ago 15.02 EST Suzanne Wrack has filed her match report from Camp Nou, and here it is: 
 Arsenal continue to be a sharp thorn in the side of the European champions, Barcelona, digging deep to hold on to a draw here. Frida Maanum put the Gunners ahead despite a hugely dominant performance from Barcelona, but Caroline Graham Hansen’s equaliser ensured the spoils would be shared.
 The last time these two teams met, Arsenal were lifting aloft the Champions League trophy at Barcelona’s expense after the most perfect of defensive performances and a Stina Blackstenius goal in Lisbon in 2025. It was a far less perfect defensive performance this time, but Arsenal showed guts against the team that retook their crown last season and showed they can play ugly when needed.
 Much more here:
 Arsenal stand firm for WCL draw in face of Barcelona dominance Read more Share 2h ago 14.54 EST Barcelona could have been five up at the break, but really Arsenal were the more dangerous side in the last half-hour. They’ll be annoyed by the equaliser as well: Taylor Hinds, the left-back, left Caroline Graham Hansen to put pressure on the ball in the middle and nobody moved across to cover the space she’d vacated. Even when Hinds might have moved back towards the Norwegian, she chose instead to stand still and just point at her. That left Graham Hansen in five yards of space inside the penalty area, and that’s all she needed.
 Share 2h ago 14.50 EST That was a really fun game of football, with lots of quality on both sides. Both goalscorers have been interviewed, starting with Barcelona’s Caroline Graham Hansen:
 double quotation mark They did a good job. Well organised. They tried to play football. It was a tough game, well done to them. We had enough chances to win the game. That’s football. It was fun to play today, we just have to keep working. They were there, blocking shots and doing a good job. Credit to them, and we know we can do better.
 And continuing with Frida Maanum:
 double quotation mark Definitely it’s a good performance from us defensively. We ran a lot, we disrupted their attacking game and we got away with a point, which against Barcelona away is [not bad]. We had 30% ball possession but I think we created lots of good chances. Overall, a good performance in terms of creating that many chances against Barca away and then performing defensively. We’re going to build from this. It’s a good performance. There’s always things we can do better.
 Share 2h ago 14.40 EST Final score: Barcelona 1-1 Arsenal
 90+3 mins: The referee pauses play and puts a hand to her ear. Is the VAR going to intervene at the very last to turn this game around? Several nervous seconds pass, but then she blows the final whistle!
 Share 2h ago 14.39 EST 90+3 mins: Arsenal hack clear. The referee waves play on.
 Share 2h ago 14.38 EST 90+2 mins: Russo has the ball on the right wing near the corner, keeps it for a while, then sends in a blind cross to nobody very much. Barcelona break, and win a corner. Seconds to play!
 Share 2h ago 14.37 EST 90 mins: Claudia Pina gets the ball on the edge of Arsenal’s area, dances into it, changes direction and dances back out of it again, before finally she is dispossessed. Two minutes’ stoppage time are indicated! 
 Share 2h ago 14.35 EST 88 mins: The corner count now stands at 10-7 in Barcelona’s favour, which given they led 10-1 at one point illustrates how much the game has changed across the second half.
 Share 2h ago 14.34 EST 87 mins: Then another cross from Smith, and this one is turned behind for another Arsenal corner.
 Share 2h ago 14.33 EST 87 mins: Arsenal work two crossing chances, the first on the left and the second on the right, but can’t find a teammate on either occasion.
 Share 2h ago 14.33 EST 86 mins: Pina and Emily Fox both go down on the edge of the D at the edge of Arsenal’s area. Barcelona think they should have a free-kick, and are not at all happy when it goes the other way.
 Share 2h ago 14.31 EST 84 mins: Smith takes on Schertenleib. Mistake. The Barca midfielder has been phenomenally good today, for all that somehow none of her many shots have gone in.
 Share 2h ago 14.29 EST 83 mins: Catley completely fluffs that one, though, and it goes straight out of play. Barcelona bring Rosalía Domínguez on for Brugts.
 Share 2h ago 14.29 EST 82 mins: Arsenal win a corner, take an age to take it – assisted by the referee wanting to warn a couple of players for pushing in the penalty area – and from it they win another one.
 Share 2h ago 14.27 EST Suzanne Wrack It feels like Arsenal have embodied the energy of the teams that had frustrated them so much in the WSL this season. This low block and attempt to just soak up the Barcelona pressure and annoy them is exactly the type of approach that has blunted them in the last few months. Perhaps if Taylor Hinds and Lisa Baum, who were being run ragged and looked exhausted, had been taken off just a few minutes earlier they might have clung onto their lead at least a little longer.
 Share 2h ago 14.25 EST 79 mins: Alessia Russo is booked for pulling back Schertenleib.
 Share 2h ago 14.25 EST 79 mins: Arsenal take off Georgia Stanway, and bring on Kyra Cooney-Cross.
 Share 2h ago 14.24 EST 78 mins: The ball is played into Barcelona’s penalty area and Cata Coll races off her line to get there, only for Maanum to reach the ball first. The Barcelona keeper forces her wide, though, and then deflects the ball behind.
 Share 2h ago 14.23 EST 76 mins: The last 15 minutes, since the goal, have certainly been Barcelona’s weakest of the game. They’re still good , obviously, but they haven’t been totally irresistible.
 Share 2h ago 14.21 EST 75 mins: Schertenleib’s shot clips a defender and the resulting spin means Misa Rodriguez spills it, but she reacts to reach the loose ball just before Pajor.
 Share 2h ago 14.18 EST 72 mins: A lovely Barcelona move ends with Camara on the byline but not quite nailing her low cross, and the chance is gone.
 Share 2h ago 14.17 EST 70 mins: For a moment Russo might have been played through down the middle, but Arsenal instead pass down the right for Smith, who wins another corner.
 Share 2h ago 14.15 EST 68 mins: Arsenal win a corner – their second – but float it harmlessly to Cata Coll in the home goal.
 Share 2h ago 14.13 EST 65 mins: And a chance for Arsenal! Smith goes down the right, hurdles Brugts’ desperate attempt to bring her down and slides the ball across to Russo, who shoots over the bar!
 View image in fullscreen Russo rues her miss. Photograph: Joan Monfort/AP Share Updated at  14.19 EST 2h ago 14.13 EST 65 mins: Aicha Camara is booked for bringing Russo down when Arsenal were attempting to launch a counter-attack.
 Share 2h ago 14.12 EST 64 mins: And so the game settles into a new phase, with slightly changed teams and obviously a changed scoreline. Time will tell how different it is to the last one.
 Share 2h ago 14.08 EST 61 mins: Arsenal bring on Ona Batlle, formerly of Barcelona, and Olivia Smith, their record signing. Taylor Hinds and Lisa Baum go off.
 Share 2h ago 14.06 EST GOAL! Barcelona 1-1 Arsenal (Graham Hansen, 59 mins)
 And finally Barcelona take one of their chances! The superb Caroline Graham Hansen is found by Brugts, chops onto her left foot and past Steph Catley, and curls the ball into the far corner!
 View image in fullscreen Caroline Graham Hansen puts the home side back on level terms. Photograph: Albert Gea/Reuters View image in fullscreen Caroline Graham Hansen is congratulated by her Barcelona teammates in front of the joyous home fans. Photograph: Álex Caparrós/Uefa/Getty Images Share Updated at  14.18 EST 2h ago 14.05 EST 58 mins: The corner ends with yet another Schertenleib piledriver, this one deflecting over the bar.
 Share 2h ago 14.05 EST 58 mins: Some really poor play from Arsenal: Misa Rodriguez’s pass plays a teammate into trouble, and her first-time blind kind-of semi-clearance gifts Barcelona the freedom of the right flank. The pull-back, though, is deflected behind.
 Share 2h ago 14.03 EST 57 mins: Ballon d’Or hogger Aitana Monmati comes on for Barcelona, and for Serrajordi.
 Share 2h ago 14.02 EST 56 mins: Maanum is booked for fouling Esmee Brugts.
 Share 2h ago 14.02 EST 55 mins: Camara’s shot is blocked, and then so is Serrajordi’s.
 Share 2h ago 14.00 EST 53 mins: Arsenal do an attack! But Foord’s cross finds only the hands of Cata Coll.
 Share 2h ago 13.59 EST 52 mins: This is going to be hard work for Arsenal. Barcelona keep pushing, Arsenal keep getting something in the way. Eventually Pina’s cross drifts out of play.
 Share 3h ago 13.56 EST 49 mins: Schertenleib overhits a cross, to such an extent that it would have dipped into the net had Misa Rodriguez not been alert.
 Share 3h ago 13.54 EST 47 mins: Arsenal could probably do with trying to take on opponents in their own penalty area a little less frequently. Stanway, I think, just did that, almost lost it, and anyway only punted it forwards a few seconds later.
 Share 3h ago 13.52 EST 46 mins: Peeeeeep! No halftimely changes as we get back under way.
 Share 3h ago 13.51 EST The players are on their way back out, Barcelona first onto the pitch. Barca were 1-0 down in the 45th minute against Atletico Madrid on Sunday and won that 2-1, so this is kind of thing nothing new for them. Can they turn this around? We’re about to find out!
 Share 3h ago 13.44 EST The moment that probably sums up the half was the way, just before the goal, the ball came off Cata Coll and then flicked up off Renee van Asten’s head, which is what meant it dropped perfectly for Maanum to score. It’s not fair to say that Arsenal are only winning because of that lucky deflection – they’re mainly winning because Barcelona have missed half a dozen amazing chances – but it’s certainly been their night so far.
 Share 3h ago 13.36 EST Half time: Barcelona 0-1 Arsenal
 45+4 mins: It’s half-time and somehow, remarkably, Arsenal have scored the only goal!
 Share 3h ago 13.35 EST 45+3 mins: Barcelona hit the post! Camara’s cross deflects across the goalmouth – could have gone anywhere – but then Arsenal give it away, it’s chipped into the box, and Graham Hansen’s glancing header bounces into the upright!
 Share 3h ago 13.34 EST 45+2 mins: Actually not a Barcelona coach but the Barcelona coach, Pere Romeu.
 Share 3h ago 13.33 EST 45+1 mins: Into stoppage time, of which there’ll be about three minutes. They start with a yellow card being shown to a Barcelona coach as the home bench whinges about a free-kick decision.
 Share Updated at  13.34 EST 3h ago 13.32 EST 45 mins: Somehow Uefa’s stats are suggesting that Arsenal lead 1-0 in “clear chances”, which is frankly bizarre. Barcelona are 16-5 up on shots, but only 3-2 on shots on target.
 Share 3h ago 13.29 EST 43 mins: Barcelona run down the other end, where Pina shoots just wide from the edge of the area.
 Share 3h ago 13.29 EST 42 mins: Arsenal touch the ball in Barcelona’s penalty area! This time, though, the pull-back is behind Maanum and it takes her too long to get her shot away.
